sections.h2: Where is Lafayette and how big is it?
sections.html:
Lafayette is the parish seat of Lafayette Parish, on the Vermilion River in the Acadiana region of south Louisiana. The city had 121,374 residents in 2020, and the consolidated city-parish had 241,753, which makes Lafayette the fourth most populous city in the state.

The metro area counted 478,384 people in 2020, the third largest in Louisiana. Lafayette sits about 135 miles from New Orleans, 59 miles from Baton Rouge and 75 miles from Lake Charles, so it works as the hub for a wide stretch of Acadiana. The parish itself covers 269 square miles and borders St. Landry, St. Martin, Iberia, Vermilion and Acadia parishes. Smaller municipalities inside it include Broussard, Carencro, Scott, Youngsville and Duson.

sections.h2: What is the history of Lafayette, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Lafayette began as the trading post of Petit Manchac and was later laid out as Vermilionville, which became the parish seat in 1824 and was incorporated in 1836. It took the Lafayette name in 1884.

Acadian refugees settled the area in the eighteenth century, which is the root of the Cajun culture the region is known for. Sugar farming drove the early economy, and the discovery of oil in the 1940s changed it. As of 2018 the city and parish had the largest number of oil and gas workers in Louisiana. The energy industry remains a big part of local employment.

Downtown has several buildings on the National Register of Historic Places, including Old Lafayette City Hall and the Cathedral of Saint John the Evangelist. Houses near the center of town can be old, and older houses carry their own repair lists.

sections.h2: What does the Lafayette economy look like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Lafayette has a mixed economy built on energy, health care, education, technology, aerospace, banking and retail. The employers listed in Wikipedia's 2021 summary include the Lafayette Parish School System, Lafayette General Health, Wood Group, Lafayette Consolidated Government, the University of Louisiana at Lafayette, Walmart, Our Lady of Lourdes Regional Medical Center, Schlumberger and Stuller.

Other large names with a presence in the area include Amazon, CGI, JPMorgan Chase, Ochsner Health System, Petroleum Helicopters International, Rouses Markets and Perficient. The University of Louisiana at Lafayette has more than 18,000 students, and South Louisiana Community College is headquartered in the city.

  • Hospitals, schools and the university are among the largest employers.
  • A campus of more than 18,000 students sits in the city.
  • Oil and gas work can move quickly with the price of crude.
  • Airport and highway access suits commuters who work in Houston or New Orleans on a rotation.

sections.h2: How do I get around Lafayette, and does it affect value?
sections.html:
Interstate 10 and Interstate 49 are the two main highways, and U.S. 90 and U.S. 167 also pass through. Lafayette Regional Airport is on the southeast side along U.S. 90, and a new passenger terminal opened on January 20, 2022.

Nonstop flights go to Atlanta, Dallas/Fort Worth, Houston and Charlotte, according to Wikipedia. The Lafayette Transit System runs local buses, Greyhound has a downtown station on Lee Avenue, and Amtrak's Sunset Limited stops on its route between New Orleans and Los Angeles. Houses near an interstate ramp are easy to reach, while houses on quieter coulee-side streets may attract buyers who prefer calm. Describe whichever fits when you talk to a buyer.

sections.h2: Is flooding a concern for a Lafayette house?
sections.html:
Lafayette lies on higher ground than much of south Louisiana. Wikipedia describes the city as part of the Prairie Terrace, higher and less wet than the wetlands to the south and west, and says it does not suffer significant flooding outside local flash flooding.

That does not make every lot safe. The city has developed on both sides of the Vermilion River, and several coulees, Isaac Verot Coulee and Coulee des Poches among them, drain into the river. Buyers and their insurers will check the flood zone, so look up the map for your address before you list and write down any past water on the property.

The climate is humid subtropical with rain all year, especially in summer. The Lafayette Regional Airport recorded a record high of 110 degrees Fahrenheit on August 27, 2023 and a record low of 4 degrees on January 22, 2025. Heat and humidity are hard on air conditioning, roofs and attic ventilation, and a hard freeze can crack pipes. Buyers may ask how old the air conditioner and roof are.

sections.h2: How are Lafayette property taxes figured?
sections.html:
The Lafayette Parish Assessor values property, and taxing bodies such as the city-parish and the school board set the rates. The assessor says state law requires reassessment at least every four years, though values can change yearly with sales.

The homestead exemption covers the first $7,500 of assessed value, which equals $75,000 of market value, and it applies to the home where the owner lives. It also covers a pool, outdoor kitchen, pool house or storage building belonging to the owner, but not a second house or a commercial building on the same land.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Lafayette assessment, and when is tax due?
sections.html:
Talk to a deputy assessor first and bring evidence that the assessment is above market value. If you still disagree, you can appeal to the Lafayette Consolidated Council at hearings held in September, then to the Louisiana Tax Commission, and after that to district court within thirty days.

Louisiana law sets December 31 as the payment deadline for each year's property tax. Unpaid taxes become delinquent the next day. If you are selling in the second half of the year, make sure the current bill is paid or settled at closing.

sections.h2: What disclosure does a Lafayette seller owe?
sections.html:
A seller of a house in Lafayette has to fill out the Louisiana property disclosure form and hand it to the buyer by the time the buyer makes an offer, under R.S. 9:3198.

The seller may say a fact is unknown. The form is not a warranty. A seller is not liable for a mistake that was not willful, or for repeating a report from a public body or licensed professional the seller reasonably trusted. If the form comes late, the buyer has 72 hours to withdraw, excluding weekends and holidays. Given the water and heat issues above, fill in the roof, plumbing, air conditioning and any water history with care.

sections.h2: What property rules does Lafayette enforce?
sections.html:
Lafayette Consolidated Government has a Property Maintenance Code, and its Compliance Division applies the code to properties in the city and in the unincorporated parish.

The Code Enforcement Section deals with tall grass, litter and debris, junked items and other nuisances, and the city-parish also regulates unsafe structures through its building code. An empty inherited house can collect a notice if the grass grows or debris piles up. Clear it, or tell a cash buyer about the notice so it can be handled at closing. Unsafe structures fall under a separate part of the building code, so ask the city-parish what applies to a damaged house.

faqs.q: Is Lafayette a city or a parish?
faqs.a: It is both. Since 1996 the city and parish have operated as one consolidated government, the Lafayette Consolidated Government, though five other municipalities keep their own governments.

faqs.q: What does the Lafayette homestead exemption cover?
faqs.a: It covers the first $7,500 of assessed value, equal to $75,000 of market value, on the home where the owner lives. It does not cover a second house or a commercial building on the same land.

faqs.q: Does the assessed value freeze pass to a buyer?
faqs.a: No. The freeze ends on sale, effective the last day of December of the year before the sale year, so the buyer's home is assessed at the current value.

faqs.q: How do I challenge my Lafayette assessment?
faqs.a: Start with a deputy assessor and bring evidence. After that you can appeal to the Lafayette Consolidated Council in September, then to the Louisiana Tax Commission.

faqs.q: Is Lafayette in a flood-prone area?
faqs.a: Parts of it drain slowly after hard rain, though the city sits on higher ground than much of south Louisiana. Check the flood zone for your own address.

faqs.q: Who enforces tall grass and debris rules?
faqs.a: The Code Enforcement Section of Lafayette Consolidated Government handles tall grass, litter, junked items and similar nuisances.
